lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- Who Is Fernando Bottura? The Career Story in English
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernando Meneghelli Bottura | Lesson 1 -- The Career Story

listenings.text: Fernando, it's Claire Doyle again. Good news, they want to move to the next stage, so I am putting a call in the diary for Thursday. There will be two people on it. The Group CFO in Brussels, who owns the numbers and will go straight into detail, and the HR director, who runs the process and will ask about your team and your style. Come prepared with two examples of a turnaround you have led, with figures, because he will ask for them. One more thing, and this is important. The whole conversation will be in English, and the Group CFO tends to interrupt with follow-up questions, so do not plan a long speech. Call me back if anything is unclear.

So, briefly. I have worked in media finance for eighteen years now, and I started as a financial analyst in Chicago, which is where I learned to read a client contract properly. I moved into agency work in 2011, and I have been a CFO since 2016. The year I always talk about is 2019, because we lost our largest client, roughly a fifth of the revenue, in a single phone call. I rebuilt the cost base over the following two quarters and we protected the margin, which nobody in the group expected. And the one thing I still have not learned to do well, honestly, is to say no to a good project quickly. I still study it for three weeks first.

extra_audio.text: Claire introduces herself and asks him to walk her through his career. Fernando says he has been at the helm of finance for fourteen years. Fernando gives the dates of his last group and the project he spearheaded there. Claire says the client is Belgian and asks how comfortable he is in English. Fernando explains what he brings to the table that a local candidate would not.
